mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which increases discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the negative correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in mortgage applications (HOUST) indicates weakening household demand but increased housing activity, which historically precedes a mild, short-lived equity rally as investors anticipate stabilization.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 3-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not statistically different from zero during triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when unemployment exceeds 6%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered instances, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and SPX declines is not significant (p > 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1% while the unemployment rate remains below 4% indicates an inflationary supply shock, which typically precedes a short-term equity pullback as investors anticipate tighter monetary policy and margin pressure.
regime_hint: tight labor market with supply disruption
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when CPIAUCSL YoY > 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 250k per month for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly above the median in triggered months, or the effect reverses when inflation exceeds 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% over three months signals a disinflationary easing cycle, which supports risk assets and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS monthly change < -0.5% AND CPIAUCSL monthly change < -0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not statistically different from zero during triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when GDP growth is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A YoY increase in real personal savings (implied by RSAFS growth > 5%) alongside a decline in consumer spending (GDPC1 flat or falling) signals a shift from consumption to savings, which historically precedes a short-term equity correction as investors anticipate weaker retail demand.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS YoY change > 5% AND GDPC1 YoY change <= 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not robust during periods of rising unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals improving manufacturing activity, which typically boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days in non-recessionary regimes.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly above the median during triggered months, or the mechanism fails when unemployment exceeds 6%.
